meta.summary: Investigated all 36 schools across school newspapers, official admissions news/blogs, JHU News-Letter, Vanderbilt Hustler, Bowdoin Orient, Swarthmore Phoenix, Miami Hurricane, GW Hatchet, Tulane Hullabaloo, Tufts Daily, Washington Square News, Daily Free Press, Huntington News, plus IvyCoach, College Kickstart, CrimsonEducation, AdmissionSight, College Transitions aggregators, plus official Common Data Sets where accessible. RESULT: 0 schools meet the 2-source independent-confirmation quality bar. The structural reality: virtually every private US institution reports a COMBINED ED1+ED2 figure in Section C of the CDS, with ED2 sub-breakdowns withheld. JHU is the only school that releases admit COUNTS by round (242 admitted ED2 to Class of 2029) but not the ED2 applicant denominator. Boston College (Class of 2028 ED2 = 28% per admissions.blog 2024-02-06) and Northeastern (single aggregator '20%' claim from 7edu) were both REJECTED — wrong class year or insufficient sourcing.

decisions.reason: NYU explicitly does not publicly disclose ED admit counts or acceptance rates for any round. Class of 2029 ED1+ED2 combined = ~25,000 applicants (10% YoY growth) but admits not published. NYU's institutional policy is to withhold ED-specific selectivity data; admissions and Washington Square News confirm this.

Tufts has not released ED1 or ED2 acceptance rate data for the past six admissions cycles per Ivy Coach. Class of 2029 reported overall rate 10.5% (3,613 / 33,400) but no ED-round breakdown. Tufts Daily article on Class of 2029 does not include ED-specific rates.

BU 2024-2025 CDS combines ED1+ED2 in Section C. Class of 2029: 6,909 combined ED applications, ~29.47% combined ED rate. BU does not break down between ED1 (Nov 1 / mid-Dec) and ED2 (Jan 4 / Feb 10) in any public reporting.

BC Class of 2029: ~5,000 combined ED1+ED2 applicants, ~30% combined rate (1,500 admits). The admissions.blog article showing '28% ED2' is dated Feb 6 2024 — that's Class of 2028, not 2029. No Class of 2029 ED2-specific publication. REJECTED single-source aggregator approach.

JHU publishes ED2 ADMIT count for Class of 2029 (242 students admitted via ED2 on Feb 14 2025) but does NOT publish the ED2 applicant denominator. Combined ED1+ED2 = 7,563 applicants / 793 admits (10.49%). Without an ED2 applicant count, computing a rate would require attribution assumptions. JHU CDS Section C combines ED1+ED2.

WashU CDS 2024-2025 reports combined ED only. Class of 2029 ED = ~25% combined; 1,197 of 1,963 enrolled came via ED. Class of 2028 = 4,817 ED apps / 1,217 admits = 25.26%. No separate ED1/ED2 figures published.

Vanderbilt Class of 2029 publishes only combined ED stats: 6,762 applicants, 891 admits, 13.2% combined ED rate. Vandy Hustler and official Vandy Admissions Blog both explicitly note ED1 and ED2 numbers are not disclosed separately. ED1 released Dec 17, ED2 released Feb 13, but counts withheld.

CMU Class of 2029 combined ED: 553 admits / 2,680 applicants = 20.63% (combined ED1+ED2). CMU does not split rounds, and the rate is also heavily school-dependent (SCS <5%, Dietrich ~24%). No ED2-specific figure published.

Northeastern has delayed publishing its 2025-2026 CDS and Huntington News reports ED stats for Class of 2029 are 'not yet released' as of fall 2025. The '600 / 6,000 = 20%' figure appeared in a single aggregator (7edu.org) with no primary source; rejected per quality bar. Class of 2028 ED was 43% combined.

Lehigh Class of 2029 combined ED: 2,040 apps, 966 admits, 47.4% combined ED rate. Class of 2028: 2,171 / 984 = 45.3% combined. Ivy Coach explicitly: 'Lehigh presents only combined figures for both rounds together'. No ED1 vs ED2 disaggregation in Lehigh admissions statistics or Brown and White coverage.

Brandeis CDS 2024-2025 reports combined ED only: 765 ED apps / 323 admits = 42.2%. Class of 2029 status: enrollment ongoing from waitlist as of May 2025; The Justice reports class statistics will be published fall 2025. No ED1 vs ED2 split.

Tulane has yet to release Class of 2029 ED-specific data per Ivy Coach. Class of 2028: 1,946 ED apps / 1,156 admits = 59.4% combined ED. Class of 2029: ~1,100 ED admits (combined, ~half the class). Tulane Hullabaloo coverage is critical of opaque ED reporting; no ED1 vs ED2 figures published.

U Rochester publishes Common Data Sets sparingly. Most recent ED data is Class of 2028: 1,385 applicants / 527 admits = 38% combined. No Class of 2029 ED data published as of late 2025. No ED1 vs ED2 separation in any source.

Miami Hurricane (Jan 2026) explicitly states: 'The University received 2,395 Early Decision applications; 1,062 applicants were admitted under Early Decision' for fall 2025 (Class of 2029). UMiami CDS combines ED1+ED2 explicitly. Combined ED1+ED2 = 44.3%. No ED2-only figure.

RPI does not publicly publish ED2-specific or combined ED stats for Class of 2029. Most recent ED data: 240 apps / 139 admits = 58% (year unclear). Ivy Coach notes 'RPI admissions could be more forthcoming' about recent ED data.
Santa Clara reports ED1+ED2+EA combined: ~12,100 early applicants, 50% admitted across all three for Class of 2029. SCU does not separate ED2 from ED1 or EA in any published statistics.
GW has not published Class of 2029 ED data. Historical GW Hatchet coverage shows combined ED rates only (~60-70% historically). No ED1 vs ED2 breakdown in GW's CDS or admissions communications.
Villanova Class of 2029 overall: 27.4%. ED data not separately published; historical combined ED ~55-56%. Villanova does not break out ED1 vs ED2 in any source.

American University has not released Class of 2029 ED-specific data. Class of 2028: 726 ED apps / 579 admits = 80% combined ED. Class of 2029 enrollment 1,700+ but no ED breakdown. AU CDS combines rounds.

Case Western Class of 2029 combined ED: 1,053 apps / 263 admits = 24.98%. Ivy Coach: 'data is a bit of a patchwork, Case Western could use a healthy dose of statistical transparency'. No ED1 vs ED2 disaggregation.
CMC Class of 2029: 22% combined ED rate (Class of 2028: 967 / 226 = 23.37%). Ivy Coach explicitly states only combined ED rates are reported; no ED1 vs ED2 split.

Hamilton Class of 2029: 13.5% overall (1,210 admitted / ~8,964). No ED data on Class of 2030 or 2029 reported per Ivy Coach. Class of 2028 combined ED: 29.4%. Hamilton Spectator does not report ED data by round.
Vassar Class of 2029 ED ~33% (combined ED1+ED2). Vassar does not publicly disclose separate ED1 and ED2 acceptance rates per Ivy Coach. Class of 2028 combined ED = 31.2%.

Davidson Class of 2029: 8,926 apps overall, 12.6% rate. ED apps = 1,232, ED enrolls = 337 (includes QuestBridge/Posse/athletes/deferred). Davidson does not officially disclose separate ED2 acceptance rates. ED1 deadline Nov 15; ED2 deadline Jan 5.

Smith Class of 2029: 22% overall, 703 enrolled. Smith has not formally published Class of 2029 ED-specific acceptance rates. Smith CDS combines ED1+ED2. ED1 mid-Dec notification, ED2 late-Jan; no round-specific data.
W&L Class of 2029 combined ED: 844 apps / 286 admits = 34%. ED1 (Nov 1) and ED2 (Jan 1) but no separate breakdown published in W&L admissions or CDS.

Haverford Class of 2029: 825 admits / 6,730 = 13.3% overall. Class of 2028 combined ED = 33.1%. Haverford 'doesn't publicly release Class of 2029 ED-specific acceptance figures with the regularity of some peer institutions' per Ivy Coach.

Colgate Class of 2029: 1,342 combined ED apps, 473 enrolled via ED (56.71% of class). One search returned '995 ED1 admits + 336 ED2 admits' but neither the official Colgate first-year profile nor Ivy Coach corroborates the 995/336 split — that single result appears to be hallucinated by the LLM cross-pollinating with Hamilton context. Until a primary source verifies, marked UNAVAILABLE.
Bates Class of 2029: 14.39% overall rate; combined ED ~40% range. Bates does not break down ED1 vs ED2 in published reports. Bates Student newspaper does not provide ED2-specific figures.

Colby Class of 2029: 7% overall (1,410 admits / 20,144). 'Colby College does not report acceptance rate data for its Early Decision application round' per College Transitions. No ED2-specific data published. Colby Echo does not break down by round.

Bowdoin Orient (Feb 14 2025 and Apr 4 2025) reports ~2,000 combined ED1+ED2 applicants and 296 combined admits = 14.8%. Both Bowdoin Orient articles explicitly do NOT separate ED1 from ED2 in their numbers. Dean comments confirm aggregate-only disclosure.

Pomona Class of 2029 combined ED: 1,726 apps / 224 admits = 12.98% (alternate source: 1,656 / 227 = 13.71% - rounding/timing diff). Pomona reports only combined ED in news.pomona.edu and CDS. No ED2-specific figure published; TSL (Pomona newspaper) coverage does not break down by round.

Middlebury Class of 2029: 11,831 apps, 13.9% overall; 519 binding admits (ED1+ED2+QuestBridge+Posse+College Track). Middlebury explicitly states 'we don't know the specific acceptance rates for Early Decision I or II'. Middlebury Campus (newspaper) does not break down by round.

Wellesley Class of 2029: 13.70% overall (1,192 admits / 8,700). Wellesley has not formally published Class of 2029 ED data. Class of 2028 combined ED: 1,033 / 308 = 29.82%. Wellesley does not publicly report separate ED2 acceptance rate.

Swarthmore Class of 2029: 7.52% overall (977 / 12,995); combined ED1+ED2 = 17.8%. Swarthmore Phoenix article explicitly does not provide separate ED1 vs ED2 figures. Dean only references aggregate ED rate.
Carleton Class of 2029: 7,449 apps, 20% overall, 518 enrolled. No ED1 vs ED2 acceptance rate published in Carleton class profile, Carletonian (newspaper), or Ivy Coach coverage.
